# PR re-review continuation

The review requirements are unchanged: verify prior threads, freshly review every changed file, and publish one `COMMENT` review only after complete coverage.

- Trusted pre-steps capture the PR head/base, every changed-file page, complete thread histories and prior reviews, including author and public-timing metadata. Helpers are checked out before capture. The input artifact is uploaded before inference; workers reuse its review context instead of refetching all review pages in every batch.
- `ReviewContinuation.cjs` assigns up to eight items/48 KB per batch and starts fresh CLI sessions using the pinned gh-aw Copilot harness. Small patches are embedded; the private input reader pages assigned thread histories and oversized patches. Each response carries a random acknowledgement token; the controller accepts completion only when those tokens match gap-free receipts bound to the captured snapshot, assignment and fresh invocation. `ReviewVerifyDelivery.ps1` verifies the receipts using a checksum-pinned PowerShell runtime staged in the sandbox's read-only actions mount. Receipts store token hashes, not the tokens. This establishes delivery through the reader, not comprehension.
- Workers use GitHub MCP for source reads and have no shell, write, task or safe-output access. The input-only stdio backend has no GitHub token or HTTP listener. Source reads are model-attested, not independently receipted; if the worker reports required content unavailable, the controller keeps it pending until completion or the deadline. Completed results stay in the controller's in-memory worklist; diagnostic checkpoints are not reloaded as authoritative progress. Unfinished items continue after a clean early exit. Clean no-progress responses reduce the assignment size but do not terminate review while time remains. Actual worker errors or the 22-minute soft deadline fail the run. The workflow retains its 25-minute limit.
- Only the controller queues outputs after every item completes. The trusted publication guard checks the Actions job result, immutable input identity, complete results, buffered-output routing, structured coverage counts and current PR/review state. Full base/head central ApiCompat baselines are compared once during trusted capture; every new suppression is inventoried independently of worker findings, without asserting that the affected API shipped GA. Publication freshness rereads PR, thread and prior-review state; mutation freshness checks PR state and affected threads without refetching unused reviews or immutable baselines. Missing or malformed required capture inputs fail closed. Existing threat-detection and skipped-write safeguards remain active. Both resolve and reopen operations wait for proof that the matching reply was applied. gh-aw remains responsible for sanitizing output text; the publication guard checks the deterministic suppression inventory without reconstructing free-form Markdown.

A completion result is still a model review conclusion, not proof of comprehension. Related-file reads and cross-file review remain required; prior reviews never substitute for a fresh changed-file result. The pinned GitHub MCP tool can fail on files over 1 MiB; an honest unavailable-source result remains incomplete. Source access and review are not independently verified, and this is not an unlimited or resumable-across-workflow-runs service.

## Validation

CI provisions the pinned gh-aw setup helpers for handler/receipt tests. PowerShell 7.5 or later must also be on PATH; set `GH_AW_REVIEW_PWSH` to use a specific executable. To run the Node suites locally, point `GH_AW_TEST_ACTIONS_DIR` at those same helpers:

```bash
GH_AW_TEST_ACTIONS_DIR=/path/to/pinned/gh-aw/setup/js node --test .github/workflows/test/*.Tests.cjs .github/workflows/test/pr-re-review-unresolve-thread.test.cjs
```

Run the Pester suites under `.github/workflows/test`, and compile `pr-re-review.md` with the pinned gh-aw version after workflow changes. Subprocess fixtures reproduce the 106-file clean early-stop case without inference or GitHub writes; they do not establish hosted end-to-end review quality.
